diagnostics.message: run() calls runlogstats.Summarize(r) and unconditionally treats scanner.Scan() returning false as end-of-input; it never checks bufio.Scanner.Err() (returned nowhere from Summarize). A path that os.Open succeeds on but subsequently fails to read (e.g. a directory, EISDIR; or any other read(2) error mid-stream) is silently treated as an empty, fully-read input: LinesRead=0, no stderr message, and exit code 0 with a printed summary block. This violates the acceptance criterion 'Exit status is 0 whenever a summary was printed, non-zero with a stderr message when the input could not be read at all' -- here the input genuinely could not be read, yet the tool reports success.

checks.test_coverage_gap: main_test.go's TestRun_UnreadablePathIsFatal only exercises a non-existent path (os.Open failure). No test exercises a path that opens successfully but fails during read (directory, permission-revoked-after-open, device error, etc.), so this defect was not caught by the existing suite.
